rules.judge: Is .output of a triggerAndWait or batchTriggerAndWait result read on a path where .ok was never checked and .unwrap() was not called? Report only that case. A read after an .ok check, or a result that is only passed on, is not a hit.
rules.message: reads .output of a triggerAndWait result before any .ok check or .unwrap() call; the child run may have failed
rules.fix: check result.ok before reading result.output, or call .unwrap() to get the output or a throw

rules.message: trigger() or batchTrigger() runs as a bare statement, without await or return, inside a task; the parent can finish before the child is queued
rules.fix: await the trigger call (or return it)

rules.message: triggerAndWait or a wait.* call is in a file that defines no task(); this looks like a route handler, outside task code
rules.fix: move the wait into a task and trigger that task from the app with tasks.trigger
rules.judge: Confirm the file is route, page or server-action code and not task code. A helper that is only ever called from inside a task() is fine; a Next.js route handler, an Express handler or a server action that awaits triggerAndWait or a wait.* call is the bug.

rules.message: trigger() runs once per loop, map or forEach item; batchTrigger sends the same items as one batch call
rules.fix: collect the payloads and call batchTrigger once

rules.judge: Is a batchTrigger call given a literal batch of more than 1,000 items, or is it made with no BatchTriggerError or isRateLimited handling on its failure path? Report only those cases. A batch built from a runtime list that is chunked, or a call whose catch branch checks BatchTriggerError, is not a hit.
rules.message: batchTrigger has a literal batch over 1,000 items, or this file has no BatchTriggerError or isRateLimited handling
rules.fix: chunk the batch to 1,000 items or fewer; catch BatchTriggerError and back off when isRateLimited is true

rules.message: triggers a task through a binding loaded with await import(); see COULD_NOT_FIND_EXECUTOR in the troubleshooting doc
rules.fix: use a top-level import, or tasks.trigger("<task-id>", payload)

rules.judge: Does a catch block inside run() log or swallow the error and then return normally, without rethrowing and without throwing AbortTaskRunError? Report only that case. A catch that rethrows, or throws AbortTaskRunError, is not a hit.
rules.message: a catch inside run() logs the error and returns normally, so the run finishes as Completed
rules.fix: rethrow the error, or throw AbortTaskRunError when a retry cannot help

rules.judge: For each error thrown in run(): is AbortTaskRunError used for a failure a retry could fix (timeout, 429, 5xx, network reset), or is a plain Error thrown for a failure no retry can fix (validation, 4xx other than 429, record not found)? Report only a clear mismatch.
rules.message: AbortTaskRunError turns off retries for that attempt; a plain Error is retried under the retry settings of the task
rules.fix: choose by retryability: AbortTaskRunError for permanent failures, a plain Error for transient ones; use catchError for per-error handling

rules.judge: Does a payment, email or charge call inside run() send no provider idempotency key? A key built from ctx.run.id or a business id is not a hit, and neither is a call that only reads data.
rules.message: a payment, email or charge call inside run() has no provider idempotency key, so a retried attempt can repeat it
rules.fix: pass a provider idempotency key built from ctx.run.id or a business id

rules.message: idempotencyKey is built from randomUUID, uuid, nanoid, Date.now or Math.random, so each trigger gets a new key and deduplication never matches
rules.fix: derive the key from a stable business id

rules.judge: Inside a task, is a raw-string idempotency key, or a key from idempotencyKeys.create() with the default scope, meant to make work happen once ever across runs? Report only that case. A key from idempotencyKeys.create() with scope "global" is not a hit.
rules.message: a raw-string idempotency key inside a task defaults to run scope, so it dedupes only within one run; once-ever needs scope "global"
rules.fix: create the key with idempotencyKeys.create(key, { scope: "global" }) when it must hold across runs

rules.judge: Look for synchronous CPU-heavy loops inside task code (parsing, hashing, image or data crunching, nested loops over large arrays) that run longer than about a minute without awaiting anything. Such a loop blocks the event loop, so heartbeats stop and the run is marked stalled after about 5 minutes. Fix: await heartbeats.yield() inside the loop, move the work to a worker thread, or use a bigger machine.
rules.message: a synchronous loop with no await in its body runs with no heartbeats.yield(); a long CPU loop can stop heartbeats
rules.fix: await heartbeats.yield() inside the loop, move the work to a worker thread, or use a larger machine

rules.message: setInterval, or setTimeout or sleep with a delay of 10 s or more, is used in a task file; the run keeps executing for the whole delay
wait.for({ seconds }) under 60 inside a polling loop; below 60 s the run keeps its concurrency slot for the whole wait
rules.fix: use an interval of 60 seconds or more, or a waitpoint token
